overview: This single-page file index records one State Department paper concerning a murder committed aboard the Japanese steamship Ragon Maru on the high seas. It summarizes an April 13 conversation between Far Eastern Division official Eugene H. Dooman and Japanese Embassy Third Secretary Shun-ichiro Kawahara about whether the Department of Justice had instructed the U.S. district attorney in Honolulu. A Justice Department official, Mr. Ramsay, reportedly concluded that no federal law appeared to have been violated, that any violation of Hawaiian territorial law was for the territorial authorities to determine, and that the ship’s master could retain custody of the accused person.

subfiles.about: An index entry summarizes an April 13 diplomatic conversation about jurisdiction and custody following a murder aboard the Japanese steamship Ragon Maru on the high seas.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Embassy Third Secretary Shun-ichiro Kawahara asked Eugene H. Dooman whether the Department of Justice had instructed the U.S. district attorney in Honolulu. Dooman consulted Mr. Ramsay of the Justice Department, who said that no federal offense appeared to have occurred and that the Hawaiian territorial authorities should determine whether territorial law had been violated. Ramsay also indicated that the vessel’s master could take custody of the accused person; the entry includes a reference to file 811s.0145.

interest: Although only an index sheet survives here, it preserves a compact account of the U.S. government’s initial jurisdictional reasoning in a homicide aboard a Japanese merchant vessel outside territorial waters. It is useful for studying the division of authority among federal officials, Hawaii’s territorial government, and a foreign ship’s master, as well as routine communication between the State Department and Japanese Embassy. The cross-reference to file 811s.0145 may help locate fuller documentation of the incident.
